claims.statement: SPINDLE, which adds a low-rank injected update W = W0 + (α/r)BA to the query and value attention projections while freezing pretrained weights, outperforms full fine-tuning on all eight GLUE tasks with RoBERTa-base while training only 0.24% of the parameters (e.g. 95.1 vs 94.8 on SST-2, 80.1 vs 78.7 on RTE, 64.1 vs 63.6 on CoLA).

An ablation on RoBERTa-base shows SPINDLE's performance on SST-2, RTE, and CoLA increases with rank r from 1 to 8 (e.g. RTE 77.3→80.1, CoLA 61.5→64.1) but slightly declines or plateaus when r is further increased to 16 (RTE 79.8, CoLA 63.9), indicating diminishing returns beyond r=8.

meta_review.summary:
The paper proposes SPINDLE, a PEFT method that freezes pretrained weights and adds a trainable low-rank update (α/r)BA to the query and value projections.
B is zero-initialised and the update is merged into the weights after training.
On RoBERTa-base/GLUE (single seed), the paper claims SPINDLE trains 0.24% of parameters, adds no inference latency, beats full fine-tuning on every GLUE task, and is the first method to do so at this budget.
A rank ablation (r=1..16) on three tasks shows saturation at r=8.

sink.text: All results come from a single seed with no variance and no significance test, yet the paper asserts the results are 'statistically robust'. Most gains over full fine-tuning are 0.2–0.6 points, on tasks such as RTE, MRPC and CoLA that are known to vary by points across seeds.

The evaluation protocol is unequal in two ways. First, SPINDLE's rank, injection sites and learning rate were selected on the same dev sets that are reported, while the baselines were left untuned. Second, the search ranges and training budgets (epochs, steps) are undisclosed for every method.

strengths.text: The no-inference-latency claim follows directly from merging the low-rank update into W0, and the 0.24% parameter fraction is consistent with Table 1.
Datasets, splits and per-task metrics are clearly disclosed, and the background citations are accurate.
The rank ablation gives a coherent picture of diminishing returns beyond r=8, though it is single-seed.

questions: How does SPINDLE differ in any respect from LoRA (Hu et al., 2021)? Why is LoRA neither cited nor compared against?
How do you reconcile the 'every GLUE task' claim with Table 1's MNLI and QQP numbers?
Can you report mean and standard deviation over at least 5 seeds, with significance tests against full fine-tuning?
Were the rank, injection sites and learning rate selected on the reported dev sets? What was the search space, and were the baselines given an equal search?
Can you provide measured optimizer memory and a quantitative ablation of the zero-initialisation and α/r scaling?
meta_review.would_change_my_mind:
That difference would need to be backed by a head-to-head comparison against LoRA under equal tuning, multi-seed results with variance, and a held-out selection split.
Absent that, the paper is a re-presentation of prior work with claims its own table contradicts.
